claim_reviews.conclusion: “Pupil of the eye” correctly cues the dark central opening in the iris.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Pupil” is a valid Indonesian term for the eye’s pupil.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Anak mata” is a valid and well-established Malaysian Malay term for the pupil.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Different-common-word” is acceptable as a learner-oriented default usage contrast, but should not imply that Malaysian Malay never uses “pupil.”
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation

claim_reviews.conclusion: No material false-friend contrast is required; the forms refer to the intended anatomical sense.

response.rationale: Both answers identify the same anatomical sense. Indonesian uses “pupil,” while Malaysian Malay uses “anak mata”; “pupil” is also attested in Malaysian Malay, so the relation is a useful default-term contrast rather than an absolute language divide. No false-friend issue is present.
